findings.title: `deleteCacheMutation` does not invalidate `connectedCalendars` query after deleting cache
findings.body: `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and invokes `onSuccess?.()`, whereas `disconnectMutation` below it invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` in `onSettled`. Because `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper` fetches `connectedCalendars` internally and its callers often do not pass an `onChanged` callback that refetches that query, `cacheUpdatedAt` will remain populated in the React Query cache after the user deletes the cache, so the dropdown continues to show the old cache status and 'Delete cached data' option until a manual page refresh. Add `await utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` in `onSettled` (or `onSuccess`) of `deleteCacheMutation`.

findings.title: `ConnectedCalendarList` receives `disableConnectionModification` instead of `shouldDisableConnectionModification`
findings.body: On line 166, `shouldDisableConnectionModification = isDisabled || disableConnectionModification` is computed and passed to `SelectedCalendarsSettingsHeading`, but line 182 passes the raw `disableConnectionModification` prop to `ConnectedCalendarList`. When `disabledScope === scope` (`isDisabled === true`) and `disableConnectionModification` is not explicitly set, `CredentialActionsDropdown` will still allow disconnecting the integration or deleting cache even though the current scope is disabled. Pass `shouldDisableConnectionModification` (or include `isDisabled`) instead.
